Calendar · AY 2025–2026

Events & seminars

The department hosts weekly seminars across the academic year, plus dissertation and thesis defenses, occasional public lectures at Hartwell Auditorium, and field-trip orientations through the summer field season.

Upcoming

Jun 25 3:00 PM
Dissertation Defense

Ezra Okonkwo-Lin — Mesoscale eddy heat transport in the Gulf Stream extension, 1993–2024

Committee chair: Prof. Mahalingam · M-302 Mendel Hall

Ezra's dissertation combines two decades of satellite altimetry, Argo float profiles, and a new ocean reanalysis to quantify how mesoscale eddies redistribute heat across the Gulf Stream extension. The public seminar is open to all; the closed oral examination follows immediately afterward.

+ Add to calendar (.ics)
Jun 30 12:00 PM
Summer Brown Bag

Working with the EAMS open-data portal: a hands-on demo

Esteban Mendoza, Lecturer in EDS · M-115 grad commons

Bring your laptop. We'll walk through accessing recent CTD data from the spring cruise, the Cobbett Point aerosol observatory's hourly stream, and an example reproducible workflow that fetches both and produces a publication-quality figure. Lunch provided for the first 25 attendees.

+ Add to calendar (.ics)
Jul 09 6:30 PM
Public Lecture

Heat domes, the Atlantic blob, and what made 2024 the hottest summer on record

Prof. Wei-Ling Tan, Atmospheric Sciences · Hartwell Aud.

The 2024 summer was the hottest on record by a substantial margin, with extreme heat events across both Northern Hemisphere mid-latitudes and a remarkable patch of warm North Atlantic SSTs. Prof. Tan will explain what we currently understand about how these patterns relate, and what they suggest about coming summers. Free, open to the public; no registration required. Q&A and reception in the atrium after.

Jul 15 9:00 AM
Field Trip Orientation

Summer field-camp orientation: EAMS 2210 Coastal Sedimentary Systems

Profs. Kasprzak & Two-Hawk (S.) · M-118 Mendel Hall

Mandatory orientation for students enrolled in the summer field session of EAMS 2210. We'll cover gear checks, safety briefings, the Cobbett Point shoreline transect, and what to expect during the four field days. Transport from Brennan to the field site is provided.

Jul 22 2:00 PM
MS Thesis Defense

Lily Tran — Trace-metal cycling in the Cobbett Bay watershed after stormwater retrofits

Advisor: Prof. Okonkwo · M-209 Mendel Hall

Lily's MS thesis quantifies how a series of municipal stormwater retrofits installed in 2019–2021 changed trace-metal fluxes from the upper Cobbett Bay watershed. Open to the EAMS community; refreshments to follow.

Aug 04 3:00 PM
Special Seminar

The eastern tropical North Pacific oxygen-minimum zone: thirty years of biogeochemistry

Dr. Carla Mendes-Almeida (LIMNOPED, Lisboa) · M-302

Dr. Mendes-Almeida visits the Singh lab for a week and will present an overview of three decades of biogeochemical observations in the eastern tropical North Pacific OMZ, with particular attention to the puzzling decadal trends in fixed-nitrogen loss.

Aug 17 10:00 AM
Field Trip Orientation

Brennan Geological Reserve summer field-camp orientation

Cormac FitzGerald, Research Scientist · M-118 Mendel Hall

Required orientation for all students enrolled in EAMS 4910 (Summer Field Camp). Covers transport to the Reserve, lodging arrangements, daily field routine, gear lists, and safety. Camp runs August 24 through September 19.

Sep 04 4:00 PM
Fall Colloquium

Opening seminar: A welcome from the Chair and a year in review

Prof. Asha Mahalingam · M-302 Mendel Hall · reception 5:15 PM

The first colloquium of the academic year. The Chair will review the past year's department milestones — recent grants, new hires, capital improvements — and outline priorities for AY 2026–27. All EAMS students, faculty, and staff are welcome. Reception in the atrium afterward.

+ Add to calendar (.ics)
Sep 11 4:00 PM
Fall Colloquium

Aerosol nucleation along sea-breeze fronts: progress and open questions

Prof. Babatunde Adeyemi · M-302 Mendel Hall

The first research colloquium of the fall. Prof. Adeyemi will present three years of tower observations at Cobbett Point, the planned expansion to Buzzards Bay, and discuss the remaining puzzles in how marine-derived aerosols form at coastal fronts.

Sep 18 2:00 PM
Qualifying Exam

Bea Schultz — PhD qualifying examination (Glaciology)

Committee chair: Prof. Two-Hawk (S.) · M-410

Bea will defend her three-chapter research proposal on subglacial hydrology at Kangerlussuaq Glacier. The qualifying defense is closed to non-committee members; please send Bea your congratulations afterward.

+ Add to calendar (.ics)
Oct 02 6:00 PM
Public Lecture

The salt marsh in a changing climate: a town-meeting conversation

Prof. Sofia Arroyo, with the Town of Brennan Resilience Office · Brennan Town Hall

A community conversation, hosted jointly by EAMS and the Town of Brennan, about what the Cobbett Marsh Observatory results mean for local shoreline management. Prof. Arroyo will give a short introduction and then take questions with the town's resilience director. All are welcome.

+ Add to calendar (.ics)
Oct 15 3:00 PM
Dissertation Defense

Marcus Holloway — Aerosol nucleation along the Massachusetts Bay sea-breeze front: a four-year tower record

Advisor: Prof. Adeyemi · M-302

Marcus presents the central results of his dissertation: four years of continuous tower-based aerosol observations along the coastal sea-breeze front, plus a comparison with shipboard sampling from two cruises. Reception to follow in the atrium.

Past events spring 2026

Recently concluded events. Recordings for the public-lecture series are available through the Hartwell Library digital archive.

Prof. Mahalingam presented results from the group's Nature Geoscience paper, including the eight-year mooring record and the longer reconstruction back to 1820. Recording available via the library archive.

The annual undergraduate research showcase, held in the Mendel Hall atrium. Three senior theses were nominated for the College of Science Hartwell Prize. Photos and abstracts archived with the registrar.

A methods-focused talk by Prof. Rasmussen on the Bayesian framework used in the new Lake Atticut reconstruction. Slides are available on the department open-data portal under talks/2026-04-rasmussen/.

Anaya defended Reorganization of Labrador Sea convection during the 1995–2018 cold blob. Anaya is taking up a postdoctoral position at Woods Hole this fall.

Prof. Emeritus Thurston gave a visually-driven public lecture on Gulf of Maine bathymetry, the geologic history of the basin, and the impact of trawling on benthic habitat. Attendance ~280. Recording available via the library archive.

A research colloquium connecting the Ito lab's melt-inclusion work at Sakurajima with a new generation of physics-based eruption forecasts. Talk slides on the open-data portal.
